title: Machine resources: RAM, processes, browsers, waits

questions.text: What is the measured peak RAM of one instance of each heavy job I will run, and how many run machine-wide right now?
Which processes, servers and browsers will I start, which handle owns each tree, and what kills it on success, failure and interrupt?
Which lock or slot will I take, and is it enforced by a hook or only by good intent?
Is there already a running server, install or browser I can reuse instead of starting another?
Which browser, profile or tab will I use, and is it isolated from the owner's own windows?
For every wait: what event, what timeout, what happens on timeout?
Does any tool or local server I add cost RAM per session, and what is the total at max sessions?
What are my budgets: wall-clock deadline, max agents, max tool calls, and who stops me? Pre-mortem: the machine froze an hour from now; what did I start?

budgets.measure: peak summed private bytes of the job's tree (mem_map / heavy_capped log)
processes started after task start whose parent is gone, plus ports still bound
automation browser processes (debugging port/pipe, non-default profile) after the task

rules.title: Kill by process name (taskkill /IM, pkill, killall)
rules.why: Kills every process with that name: other agents, the owner's tools, the agent host itself.
rules.confirm: static-proof: the command is in a script
rules.fixHint: kill the tree you started by PID (taskkill /PID <pid> /T /F, kill -- -<pgid>) or a Job Object

rules.title: while-true sleep loop (busy wait with no exit or deadline)
rules.why: Waits forever or polls blindly; holds a slot and hides a stall.
rules.confirm: repro-script: run with the awaited event never happening; it never exits
rules.fixHint: wait on the event (process exit, health endpoint with a deadline, a watcher) with an explicit timeout

rules.title: Browser/context launched with no close in finally or fixture teardown
rules.why: Windows pile up and eat RAM; a crash leaves them open.
rules.confirm: measurement: automation browser count after the run > 0

rules.title: Promise.all / & / background over heavy jobs with no concurrency limit
rules.why: Peak RAM = jobs x peak per job; the machine swaps or crashes.
rules.confirm: measurement: peak commit during the run vs the budget

rules.title: Typecheck/build/install outside the machine-wide lock
rules.why: Advisory locks only work when everyone takes them.
rules.confirm: repro-script: guard log shows the command without the wrapper

rules.title: Agent spawn loop with no cap or deadline passed to children
rules.why: Agents multiply and outlive the task.
rules.confirm: measurement: live agents vs the cap during the run

verify.text: no process from this task alive (PID tree, start time, command line); ports released
automation browser processes = 0; tabs I created closed; owner tabs untouched
every heavy command ran under the wrapper (guard log violations = 0)
peak RAM / commit %, concurrent heavy jobs, agents spawned, wall-clock vs deadline
no bare sleeps; every wait has a timeout
